title: Scheduling: node selectors, affinity and anti-affinity

videos.script: So far the scheduler has chosen every node on its own, looking only at requests. Usually that is what you want. {{own}} Sometimes it is not. A search service needs the fast disks. Three copies of the shop should not share one machine, because one machine can fail. A helper should sit next to the thing it helps. {{cases}} Each of these is a rule you can write in the pod. Some rules are requirements, and a pod that cannot meet one waits. Others are preferences, and the scheduler bends them when it has to. {{kinds}} You will label a node, pin pods to it, ask for something no node has, and then spread three copies across two machines and watch the third one wait. {{plan}}
